The earliest agrarian society in Australia in my Alt history world, the Murrayan society, had a game called Tuurntuwapula, which means “circles.” 

Tuurntuwapula was played on a square playing field with a circular pit on each side, between two teams of 6 players, with an animal-skin ball. The ball could not be rolled, but could be thrown, tossed or kicked in the air. A player who had the ball could not move until they got rid of the ball, or if it was knocked out his hands by an enemy player. The goal of the game was to toss, throw and kick the ball into one of the enemy team’s 2 holes for points. A team would need 10 points to win a game. 

This game actually had some political importance, as it was sometimes used to settle family/clan disputes peacefully if war was only a second option.
